label: Dupilumab (Dupixent) — asthma · Zhang 2021 · 2-compartment SC · linear + Michaelis-Menten
_note: Second dupilumab model: asthma (adults and adolescents), fitted in one step with no fixed parameters. Same parameterisation as the FDA atopic dermatitis model, but its own values - notably Km 2.08 mg/L instead of 0.01.

_source.document: Zhang et al. 2021, CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 10:941-952 (doi:10.1002/psp4.12667, PMC8376131)
_source.table: Table 3: final model parameters; Results: covariate equations; Table 2: population; Table 4 and Figure 3: exposures
_source.subjects: N=2114 (202 healthy volunteers, 1912 asthma patients incl. 68 adolescents), 14,584 concentrations; phase 1 IV 1-12 mg/kg and SC 75-600 mg, phase 2a/2b and phase 3 QUEST

_parameterisation.why: The paper estimates Ke, V2, K23, K32 (rates) and Vmax as a concentration rate, like the FDA model. The engine works in CL/Q/Vp:
_parameterisation.consequenceForCovariates: Weight and albumin on V2 therefore move Vc, CL, Q and Vp by the same factor; weight, CrCL and ADA on Ke move CL only.
_parameterisation.Vm: Vmax 1.39 mg/L/day is multiplied by each subject's Vc to give an amount rate.

limitations: Correlations between the between-subject variabilities are not reported in the paper, so all are sampled independently.

The paper does not say which transformation (exponential/logit) the between-subject variability in bioavailability (F) (CV 36.3%) uses, so it is applied exponentially and truncated at 1 when it exceeds 1.
202 healthy subjects and asthma patients were fitted together, and population (healthy/asthma) is not a covariate.
The reference-subject validation values (Table 4) are patient means, so they inherently differ from the value for a single reference subject (the distribution is right-skewed, so the mean is higher).
The source gives no intervals for the percentage change in AUC by weight, so ±20% is used as the pass criterion.
